subject: Renewal: EU data residency + APAC rollout / cross-region failover plan
messages:
From: Lena Müller <lena.mueller@eurehealth.de>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:12:00 +0200
Subject: Renewal and EU data residency + APAC readiness

Hi Naomi,

Our renewal window is coming up and the leadership team has made two requests we need covered in the new term:

1) Move our primary data residency for production PII to the EU region (we currently run in us-west). We need confirmation that all inference logs, embeddings, and user content can be kept in eu-central-1 and that the contract reflects that.

2) We want a phased APAC rollout for latency-sensitive clinics in Japan and Australia. Primary ask: an operational runbook for cross-region failover (APAC <-> EU) and cost/pricing for adding APAC region capacity.

Procurement has asked for the estimated timeline and any SLA/startup uplift for adding regions. Renewal is targeted for 3 weeks from now (31 May).

Can you please share the plan, high-level pricing, and any docs (SOC2, DPA language) we should attach to our procurement packet?

Thanks,
Lena Müller
Head of Platform Ops
EureHealth GmbH

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lena Müller <lena.mueller@eurehealth.de>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:04:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Renewal and EU data residency + APAC readiness

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear ask.

High level response up front: we can support EU data residency as part of the renewal amendment (data processing addendum + contract language) and we can stage an APAC rollout with cross-region failover. I’ve looped in Jordan (commercial lead), Marcus (solutions), and Monica (CS/onboarding) so we can align technical approach, pricing, and timelines.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Quick sync (30 min) this week to confirm residency scope (which datasets must be EU-only: embeddings, audit logs, backups?)
- Marcus will draft the recommended failover topology and pilot timeline.
- Jordan will prepare an amendment + uplift estimate for reserved capacity in eu and apac for the renewal term.
- I’ll package SOC2/DPA docs and a short term-sheet for procurement.

I attached a one-page renewal_term_summary_v1.pdf that outlines the options we typically present (term length vs. discount vs. reserved capacity uplift).

Are you available Wed 11 May 09:00 CET / 08:00 BST for a quick call?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: renewal_term_summary_v1.pdf (pdf, 1 page)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Lena Müller <lena.mueller@eurehealth.de>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:37:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Renewal and EU data residency + APAC readiness

Lena & team — quick technical summary and constraints from the infra side.

Summary:
- EU residency: We can pin production tenant data (user payloads, embeddings, and inference logs) to eu-central-1. This includes encryption keys managed via your KMS in the EU if you choose our private deployment or KMS integration.
- APAC rollout: We recommend an active-primary in EU with an APAC read-replica for low-latency inference; during failover we promote APAC to primary. That limits replication scope to model weights and cached KV layers; we do NOT replicate full audit trails in real time (those remain written to EU by default unless a separate retention path is requested).
- Cross-region failover profile: expected RTO ~3-10 minutes depending on warm cache and model loading profile. Warm standby with warmed KV cache reduces tail latency.

Limitations & considerations:
- Real-time global write replication for audit logs is not currently supported; we can provide an export pipeline (near-real-time) to a customer-managed EU S3 bucket if absolute EU-only storage is required for logs.
- Cold-start model loading in APAC will add latency for the first few minutes unless reserved capacity is purchased (recommended for production clinics).

Pilot timeline (8-10 weeks):
1) Week 1-2: Contract amendment + DPA sign-off; identify EU S3/KMS endpoints.
2) Week 3-4: APAC infra provisioning, reserved capacity sizing, model variant tests.
3) Week 5-6: Pilot exchange traffic to APAC region for subset of clinics.
4) Week 7-8: Full rollout and failover runbook handover.

I’ve attached a simple architecture diagram (architecture_diagram_apac_failover.png) showing active EU / warm APAC + promotion path.

If you can confirm:
- which logs must remain exclusively in EU,
- expected concurrent requests for APAC peak (req/s) or QPS per clinic,
we’ll firm up the capacity numbers.

- Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: architecture_diagram_apac_failover.png (png, 1.2MB)
From: Lena Müller <lena.mueller@eurehealth.de>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ryu Tanaka <ryu.tanaka@orionhealth.jp>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Renewal and EU data residency + APAC readiness

Thanks Naomi/Marcus — helpful summary. A few clarifications:

- Logs: Audit logs + PII-level transcripts must remain in EU. We can accept near-real-time export as long as the retention and primary copy are in EU and the contract language specifies EU-only storage for those artifacts.
- APAC sizing: for Japan launch we expect an initial peak of ~120 rps across 15 clinics, then scale to 350 rps in 3 months. For Australia we expect smaller load initially.
- Procurement timeline: we still need SOC2 summary and the DPA language to circulate with our legal team. If possible, please bundle the SOC2 summary and a redlined DPA alongside the renewal amendment.

I’m available for the Wed slot you proposed (11 May 09:00 CET) — I can also add Ryu from our integration partner in Tokyo for APAC-specific questions.

Best,
Lena

Hi Lena — following our call and the notes above, next steps and deliverables from Redwood:

1) Commercial amendment: Jordan will send a renewal amendment (term + reserved capacity uplift options) and the DocuSign link for signatures. Expect the draft in the next 24 hours.
2) Legal / compliance: I attached a short SOC2 summary (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf) and we’ll include a redlined DPA that ensures audit logs + PII remain stored in EU primary buckets.
